questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

A group of eight piano students were given one week to practise a piece for their diploma exam. The following table shows the number of hours, h, each student practised and the mark, D, awarded for their diploma exam.

[Table: h=28, 13, 45, 33, 17, 29, 39, 36; D=115, 82, 120, 116, 79, 101, 110, 121.]

(a) Find Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient, r. [2]

(b) The regression line of D on h can be written in the form D=ah+b. Find the value of a and the value of b. [1]

(c) Use the regression equation to predict how the diploma exam mark will change for every five extra hours of practice. [2]
questions.solution: (a) r=0.883529…≈0.884. (b) Regression D=1.36609…h+64.5171…, so a=1.37,b=64.5. (c) A 5-hour increase predicts 5a=6.83045…, about 7 marks higher.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let f(x)=e^(−x²)−0.5 for −2≤x≤2.

(a) Find the roots of f. [2]

(b) Sketch the graph of f on the supplied grid. [3]
questions.summary: Find and sketch an even exponential function.
questions.solution: (a) e^(−x²)=1/2 gives x²=ln2, so x=±√ln2≈±0.833. (b) The graph is even, smooth and bell-shaped, with maximum f(0)=0.5, roots ±0.833, and endpoints f(±2)=e⁻⁴−0.5≈−0.482.

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

The following diagram shows a triangle ABC where AC=12, CB=7 and BÂC=25°.

[Diagram not to scale: triangle ABC with AC=12, CB=7 and angle BAC=25°.]

Find the smallest possible perimeter of triangle ABC.
questions.solution: By sine rule, sinB/12=sin25°/7, so sinB=12sin25°/7=0.724488. Thus B≈46.426° or 133.574°. Then C≈108.574° or 21.426°. The smaller AB occurs with C≈21.426°: AB=7sinC/sin25°=6.05068…. Minimum perimeter=12+7+6.05068=25.0507≈25.1.

4. [Maximum mark: 7]

A manufacturer produces lamps. The probability that a lamp is defective is 0.05. A random sample of 30 lamps is selected.

(a) Find the probability that at least one lamp is defective. [3]

(b) Given that at least one lamp is defective, find the probability that at most two lamps are defective. [4]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows a semicircle with centre O and radius r. The points P and Q are the endpoints of a diameter, so PQ=2r. The point R lies on the semicircular arc and RÔQ=θ, where 0<θ<π.

[Diagram: two shaded regions in the semicircle—a circular segment between chord RQ and arc RQ, and a triangular region on the other side of OR.]

(a) Given that the areas of the two shaded regions are equal, show that θ=2sinθ. [5]

(b) Hence, find the value of θ. [1]
questions.summary: Equate circular segment and triangle areas.
questions.solution: (a) Segment RQ area is (1/2)r²(θ−sinθ). The other shaded triangle has area (1/2)r²sin(π−θ)=(1/2)r²sinθ. Equality gives θ−sinθ=sinθ, hence θ=2sinθ. (b) The nonzero solution on (0,π) is θ=1.89549…≈1.90 rad.

6. [Maximum mark: 9]

The sum of the first n terms of a geometric sequence is given by Sₙ=Σ from r=1 to n of (2/3)(7/8)^r.

(a) Find the value of the first term, u₁. [2]

(b) Find S∞. [3]

(c) Find the least value of n such that S∞−Sₙ<0.001. [4]
questions.summary: Sum a geometric series and bound its tail.

7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Points A and P are on opposite banks of a river. AP=65 km is perpendicular to PB=215 km. A boat travels at 42 km h⁻¹ and a bus travels along PB at 84 km h⁻¹.

[Diagram not to scale: right triangle APB with AP=65 km perpendicular to PB=215 km; D lies on PB and BD=x.]

(a) Find the total travel time if
(i) the boat travels from A to P and the bus travels from P to B;
(ii) the boat travels directly from A to B. [4]

Point D lies on PB, with BD=x km. The boat travels from A to D and the bus travels from D to B.

(b) (i) Find an expression for the total travel time T(x).
(ii) Find the value of x for which T is a minimum.
(iii) Find the minimum value of T. [6]

The boat costs $200 per hour and the bus costs $150 per hour.

(c) (i) Find the value of x for which the total cost is a minimum.
(ii) Find the minimum total cost. [4]

8. [Maximum mark: 13]

The height, H metres, of the water in a harbour t hours after midnight can be modelled by H(t)=a sin(b(t−c))+d. The first high tide is at 04:30 and the next high tide is 12 hours later. The height ranges from 2.2 m to 6.8 m.

[Graph: sinusoidal harbour height during the first 13 hours after midnight, with a maximum of 6.8 m at t=4.5 and a minimum of 2.2 m.]

(a) Show that b=π/6. [1]

(b) Find the value of a. [2]

(c) Find the value of d. [2]

(d) Find the smallest possible value of c. [3]

(e) Find the height of the water at 12:00. [2]

(f) Find the number of hours in a 24-hour period for which the tide is above 5 m. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Period 12 gives b=2π/12=π/6. (b) a=(6.8−2.2)/2=2.3. (c) d=(6.8+2.2)/2=4.5. (d) A maximum occurs when b(4.5−c)=π/2; with b=π/6, 4.5−c=3, so smallest c=1.5. (e) H(12)=2.3sin[(π/6)(10.5)]+4.5=2.87365…≈2.87 m. (f) Solve H=5 in each period: t≈1.9185 and 7.0815 around the first high tide, so duration above 5 per 12 h is 5.16295 h; over 24 h it is 10.3259≈10.3 h.

9. [Maximum mark: 16]

The random variable X is normally distributed with mean μ and standard deviation σ.

(a) Find P(μ−1.5σ<X<μ+1.5σ). [3]

The weights of avocados are normally distributed. The probabilities for the four categories are shown below.

[Table: category probabilities—small: 0.04; medium: 0.576; large: 0.288; premium: 0.096. The maximum weight for a small avocado is 106.2 g and the minimum weight for a premium avocado is 182.6 g.]

(b) Find μ and σ. [5]

A supermarket buys only avocados with weights greater than 106.2 g.

(c) Find the conditional probabilities that an avocado bought by the supermarket is medium, large and premium. [4]

The selling prices for medium, large and premium avocados are $1.10, $1.29 and $1.96 respectively. The supermarket pays $200 for a consignment.

(d) Find the minimum number of avocados that must be sold for the expected net profit to be at least $438. [4]
questions.summary: Use normal quantiles and expected revenue.
